facts.fact: VolumeGrids.save(filepath) writes a .vdb from the evaluated volume (the modifier's result); on the original data-block it also returns True and writes a file, but one with no grids in it
the bundled openvdb module reads the saved file: one FloatGrid 'density', its active voxel count, value range, voxel size, and 1.0 at the sphere's centre
bpy.ops.object.volume_import runs headless (no override) and makes a Volume object whose grids load from the file
the data API route: volumes.new + volume.filepath; the grids are listed only after grids.load(); grid.load() returns True, yet that grid's is_loaded still reads False on the original data-block
a missing file does not raise: grids.load() returns False and grids.error_message says why

a level set written with openvdb (grid 'surface', radius 0.8) loads in Blender; Volume to Mesh reads the grid named in grid_name ('density' by default), so it returns nothing until grid_name is set; at threshold 0 the surface sits at the level set's radius (0.800), at the default 0.1 it sits 0.1 m further out (0.900)

importing numbered files (seq_0001..0003.vdb) as one selection makes one Volume object that is a sequence of 3 frames; each frame loads its own file, and past the end (frame 5) none loads (sequence_mode CLIP)
